findings.title: Team admin/owner check requires both roles
findings.body: isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed with && between isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner. A team admin who is not also the owner (and an owner who is not also an admin) is treated as unauthorized. Unless that user is the booking host or already an attendee, addGuests throws FORBIDDEN, so the people who manage team event types cannot add guests.

findings.title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials, not the host's
findings.body: updateCalendarAttendees is invoked with an EventManager built from ctx.user and getUsersCredentials(ctx.user). The mutation also allows attendees (and is intended to allow team admins) to add guests, and the booking query already loads the host's credentials but never uses them. When the caller is not the host, the organizer's destination calendar is updated with the wrong user's integrations, so the invite is not updated or a different calendar is written.

findings.title: Guest dedupe and blacklist are case-sensitive
findings.body: Existing attendees are excluded with guest === attendee.email, and BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS is lowercased but the submitted guest is not. Mixed-case copies of an existing attendee are inserted again, and a blacklisted address can be added by changing letter case. Those addresses are then stored and included in calendar and email fan-out, including the meeting link.

findings.title: Emails are keyed off the raw guest list, not the guests actually added
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails is called with the original guests array after uniqueGuests has already dropped duplicates and blacklisted addresses. In sendAddGuestsEmails, any attendee whose email is in that raw list is sent AttendeeScheduledEmail (a new-booking confirmation) instead of AttendeeAddGuestsEmail. Re-submitting an existing attendee therefore sends them a fresh scheduling email and ICS REQUEST, while the database insert skipped them.

findings.title: Attendees are committed before calendar/email, so a failed retry cannot finish the job
findings.body: booking.update createMany runs before updateCalendarAttendees and sendAddGuestsEmails, with no transaction. If the calendar update throws, the mutation fails after the rows exist and emails never send. A retry then filters those emails out as already present, hits uniqueGuests.length === 0, and throws BAD_REQUEST, so the calendar and notifications stay permanently out of date.

findings.title: No checks for booking status, disableGuests, or seat capacity
findings.body: Any organizer, attendee, or (broken) team admin can add an unbounded guest list to any booking id, including cancelled, rejected, and past bookings, and event types with guests disabled. Seated event types are not checked against seatsPerTimeSlot or BookingSeat; guests are inserted as normal attendees and then emailed the video URL. That bypasses event-type policy and can overfill seated events or leak meeting links from cancelled bookings.

findings.title: Add-guest emails ignore disableStandardEmails
findings.body: sendAddGuestsEmails always emails the organizer, every team member, and every attendee. Sibling helpers (sendLocationChangeEmails, sendScheduledEmails, etc.) skip host or attendee mail when event type metadata sets disableStandardEmails. This path never receives that metadata, so event types that disabled standard mail still blast new-guest and full scheduled emails, including ICS attachments.
